You can use 70+ Adobe tools without leaving ChatGPT now – here’s how
Adobe's new plugin works both in Work and Codex, and is available today in ChatGPT.
Radhika Rajkumar
Senior Editor
Radhika Rajkumar is a senior editor at ZDNET based in New York City.…
Read full bio
Radhika Rajkumar
Senior Editor
Read full bio
August 6, 2026, 1:00 pm ET
2 min read
Elyse Betters Picaro / ZDNET
Follow ZDNET:
Add us as a preferred source
on Google.
ZDNET’s key takeaways
Adobe’s new plugin for ChatGPT puts the company’s tools directly in Work and Codex.
Design software must adapt around competitive AI products.
The SaaSpocalypse still hasn’t arrived.
Adobe is expanding its partnership with OpenAI’s
ChatGPT
through a new integration: an
Adobe for ChatGPT plugin
.
The new tool lets users access Adobe-quality creative tools via the interface many have become accustomed to for everything from search to coding. The plugin works in both
Work
and
Codex
, and is available today in the ChatGPT web and app.
More from ZDNET
Also:
I loved ChatGPT Desktop until OpenAI gutted it to make room for Codex and Work
“Drawing on more than 70 tools across Adobe’s creative and productivity suites, the Adobe plugin in ChatGPT supports a wide range of workflows, from editing photos and creating campaign videos to designing marketing assets and generating polished PDFs — all through rich, interactive experiences right in the flow of the conversation,” Adobe said in the release.
While ZDNET has yet to test the plugin, Adobe said it unifies and builds on the company’s existing ChatGPT apps, which include Photoshop, Express, and Acrobat. Adobe
made these apps available for free in ChatGPT
in December, marrying the ease of conversational instruction users have come to expect with the sophistication and specificity of Adobe’s tools, much of which AI image tools can’t match yet.
The plugin aims to keep design-related tasks, such as resizing social videos or turning data into infographics, within a single interface without sacrificing access to Adobe’s tools. An Adobe spokesperson clarified to ZDNET that some of the company’s suite of tools will be available to everyone via the plugin, but that others will be dependent on a user’s Adobe account. Free account holders, for example, will have usage limits.
Also:
I asked ChatGPT Images 2.0 to redesign my app UIs – and wow
“When you want advanced editing, creative control or pixel-level precision, you can continue your work in Adobe’s apps right where you left off,” Adobe’s announcement added. Inside its ecosystem of products, Adobe also has its own
AI assistants
, which live in Photoshop, Express, and Firefly to help with conversational edits and tasks. Adobe also has integrations with
Anthropic’s Claude
and
Microsoft Copilot
.
A changing design market
As AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic continue to release AI-powered design tools, legacy creative software companies are figuring out where they fit. Given the copyright concerns many businesses have over AI-generated images and video, Adobe’s
licensed training data
and ability to restrict tools to a company’s IP position its technology as a commercially safer option.
An Adobe employee told ZDNET on background that licensed training data still seems to matter to enterprise clients, but that the issue is also not very relevant, as tools like Claude Design haven’t emerged as a major competitor yet. They added that while Adobe staff do use some Claude tools internally, Claude Design isn’t one of them.
Also:
I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous
Overall, Adobe’s expertise in creative software appears to be keeping the business afloat. Despite
market valuations dipping
over
concerns that AI labs will make SaaS extinct
, the company continues to report
strong earnings
each quarter. The Adobe employee added that while stock fluctuations are causing some discomfort internally, morale remains high — and the plugin is further evidence that labs like OpenAI still need what Adobe has to offer.
